clues.text: This small town sits in Portugal. It lies by a bay, with the sea close at hand.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside Portugal and its coast

source.quote: Buarcos is a freguesia (civil parish) in Figueira da Foz Municipality, Portugal.

clues.text: Strong winds come from the north here, but a small range of hills blocks them. So the beach stays calm and snug.
clues.narrowing: rules out unsheltered coasts exposed to strong northern winds

source.quote: It is a traditional fishing town that has grown also as a noted beach resort due to its natural landscape namely the beach which is sheltered from the strong northern winds by the Boa Viagem small mountain range (Serra da Boa Viagem).

clues.text: In the 1600s, pirates kept raiding this town, so the people built a long wall to keep them out. It still stands today.
clues.narrowing: rules out places with no pirate raids and no 1600s fortification

source.quote: During the 1600s, the people of Buarcos were harassed by pirates and built the long fortification that stands to this day.

clues.text: This is a true fishing town, not just a beach stop for guests. Many of its people still catch fish for a living today.
clues.narrowing: rules out beach resorts where fishing is no longer a living for locals

source.quote: Many of its inhabitants still work in the fishing industry but tourism is also an important activity.

clues.text: One long beach runs along the front of this town. Bars and seafood spots look out over the bay beside it.
clues.narrowing: confirms the place by its extensive beach and bay-front bars

source.quote: It has hotels, seafood restaurants and bars with view over the bay and the extensive beach.
